fields.flaw: Equation (8): for 1 ≤ k ≤ n, ∑_{j=1}^n x_j e_k(X \ {x_j}) = k e_k(X).

0004 | 
0005 | The tools are [[Viète's Formulas]], [[Recursion Property of Elementary Symmetric Function]], [[Definition:Telescoping Series|telescoping sums]] and  [[Definition:Homogeneous Function|homogeneous functions]] of degree $k$.
0006 | 
0007 | === Details ===
0008 | 
0009 | Discovery of formulas (1)-(2) has humble beginnings:
0010 | 
0011 | {{begin-eqn}}
0012 | {{eqn | n = 3
0013 |       | l = \prod_{r \mathop = 1}^n \paren { x - x_r } 
0014 |       | r = \sum_{i \mathop = 0}^n \paren {-1}^{n-i} {\map {e_{n - i} } X} x^i
0015 |       | c = [[Viète's Formulas]]
0016 | }}
0017 | {{end-eqn}}
0018 | 
0019 | Create $n$ equations all with {{LHS}} zero by substitution  $x = x_j$ in (3), $1 \le j \le n$.
0020 | :$\ds 0 = \sum_{i \mathop = 0}^n \paren {-1}^{n-i} {\map {e_{n - i} } X} x_j^i$
0021 | Then multiply the $j$th equation by $x_j^r$ and add the $n$ equations, for $1 \le j \le n$:
0022 | 
0023 | {{begin-eqn}}
0024 | {{eqn | n = 4
0025 |       | l =  0 
0026 |       | r = \sum_{j \mathop = 1}^n \sum_{i \mathop = 0}^n \paren {-1}^{n - i} \map {e_{n - i} } X x_j^{i + r}
0027 | }}
0028 | {{eqn | r = \sum_{i \mathop = 0}^n \paren {-1}^{n - i} \map {e_{n - i} } X \map {p_{i + r} } X
fields.witness: Take n=2, k=1, x₁=1, x₂=2, and X={1,2}. The hypothesis holds: 1≤1≤2. Using e₁(S)=the sum of elements of S, e₁(X\{x₁})=2, e₁(X\{x₂})=1, and e₁(X)=3.
